message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: CI Web

on:
  workflow_call:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - .github/workflows/ci-web.yml
      - .github/workflows/cd-web.yml
      - .dockerignore
      - deploy/web/**
      - package.json
      - pnpm-lock.yaml
      - pnpm-workspace.yaml
      - vite.config.ts
      - daemon/**
      - web/**
      - apps/admin/**
      - packages/crawler/**
      - packages/translator/**

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-web-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build:
    name: CI Web
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5

    env:
      VP_GIT_HOOKS: '0'

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Lint workspace
        run: pnpm exec vp lint

      - name: Type-check and build
        run: pnpm build

      - name: Type-check applications
        run: pnpm typecheck

      - name: Unit tests (without live crawler requests)
        run: pnpm test:unit
",
  "rationale": "The workflow currently has a 30-minute timeout, but historical runs complete in 35-72 seconds. The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern recommends bounding jobs with a custom timeout based on representative successful-duration history, with operational headroom. The experiment example (batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508) demonstrates that adding a 5-minute timeout to a similar job reduced median elapsed time by 26.8% by preventing runaway consumption. Reducing the timeout from 30 to 5 minutes provides a tight bound (4-8x observed max) while preserving all build and test coverage.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508"]
}
